feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration-7 build (score 162.45, the best raced design) with one change: controller.kd from 0.4 to 0.35. Geometry (sensors at y=0.07, x from -0.05 to 0.05, weights [-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1], sensor_size 0.012), kp 3.0, ki 0.2, base_speed 1.0 and line_loss 'last_direction' are unchanged, so the race isolates damping.

Evidence: iteration 4 versus iteration 3 (same controller except kd 0.3 to 0.4) raised progress on every track (oval 0.12 to 0.48, s-bend 0.15 to 0.26, slalom 0.11 to 0.125), but it also raised oval steering_oscillation (0.075 to 0.283) and s-bend oscillation (0.139 to 0.202). Iteration 7 kept kd 0.4 and kp 3.0 and scored best. Iteration 6 showed that ki 0.3 lowered the score (oval progress 0.666 to 0.571), so ki stays at 0.2. Iteration 5 showed that forward sensors (y 0.05 to 0.07) raised oval and s-bend progress, so geometry stays.

The kd 0.35 test is a fair middle-point check. It is a small move from the best build and tests whether oscillation can fall while progress holds. Survival still comes before speed, so base_speed stays at 1.0.

Read the next race as follows. If oval progress stays near 0.74 and s-bend near 0.31 with oval steering_oscillation below 0.341, keep kd 0.35 and try controller.kp 3.5, since max_error has stayed near 0.06 and the kp 2.5 to 3.0 step was the first gain step that did not hurt. If progress falls below about 0.67 on the oval or 0.31 on the s-bend, return kd to 0.4, because the progress gain from damping outweighs the oscillation cost. Do not raise base_speed while any track ends off track early.
